title: Regional continuity simulator: Terraform modules + automated private-deploy failover rehearsals
creator: Marco Li
description:
Summary:
Build a safe, reusable Terraform/IaC module set and an automation harness that executes repeatable multi-region failover rehearsals for Private (VPC) deployments. The goal is to give customers and internal SREs a repeatable, auditable tool that conducts controlled failovers (simulated outages) for Redwood private stacks: performs pre-checks, executes the failover (routing / control-plane switch / workload relocation), validates health and metrics, and performs a safe rollback or post-mortem capture if thresholds are exceeded.

Background / why now:
- Private customers increasingly require demonstrable continuity exercises for compliance and procurement (SOC/ISO).
- Current DR playbooks are ad-hoc, manual, and fragile across customer VPC topologies and cloud providers.
- We need a Terraform-native solution that can be used by our Private team during onboarding, by our Solutions Engineers during acceptance testing, and by SREs for recurring rehearsal cadence.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
- Provide a modular Terraform package (modules/drill-runner, modules/traffic-generator, modules/bastion-proxy) that can be instantiated safely in customer-managed VPCs or Redwood-managed sandboxes.
- Define a standard automation harness (lambda/step-function or GH Actions runner) that sequences: pre-checks -> staged failover -> validation -> rollback/reporting.
- Instrument a set of health checks specific to inference (API /health, p50/p95 latency, token error rate, KV cache hit ratio, model warm-start latency) and platform checks (node counts, GPU readiness, grpc/connectivity).
- Surface drill results in Console (Drill dashboard) and attach logs/metrics to a run artifact (S3/GCS) and to a GitHub PR for auditability.
- Ensure drills are safe: require explicit gating flags, scoped IAM, time-window enforcement, and auto-rollback when safety thresholds exceeded.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement permanent DR routing changes for customer environments; it produces temporary, reversible changes and a documented operator workflow.
- We will not attempt to cover every customer network topology on first pass; initial support targets AWS VPCs with Transit Gateway and peering patterns common to our private customers.

Implementation approach / proposed components:
1) Terraform modules (src: modules/*):
   - modules/drill-runner: manages ephemeral state for a single drill (locks, run metadata, run IAM role, SQS/StepFunction wiring).
   - modules/traffic-generator: creates a sandbox ECS/Fargate or k8s job that can generate synthetic inference traffic with configurable templates and identity keys.
   - modules/bastion-proxy: ephemeral bastion and temporary route control resources (security-group updates, route table overrides) used for safe controlled failover steps.
   - modules/health-checks: reusable health-check definitions (CloudWatch Synthetic, Prometheus job, or HTTP checks) that map to Redwood health signals.
   - modules/cleanup: idempotent tear-down utilities and state-exchange hooks for reporting.

2) Automation harness (orchestration):
   - Step Function driven by an operator or scheduled GH Action. Steps: acquire lock -> run preflight checks (disk, node count, KV health) -> warm models (prefix cache) -> execute targeted routing change or instance drain -> run validation traffic -> evaluate validation rules -> rollback if thresholds breached -> publish report.
   - Simple alternative: a GH Action workflow using infra tooling for customers that cannot run StepFunctions.

3) Health and validation rules (config-driven):
   - API health: /health 200 with JSON {status: "ok"}.
   - Latency: p50 increase <= 30%, p95 increase <= 100% over baseline (baseline computed from last 1h).
   - Error rate: user-visible 5xx rate < 0.2% absolute increase.
   - KV cache hit ratio: > 60% post-warm for models that expect cached KV.
   - Token generation sanity checks: non-empty logits, non-truncated responses for canonical prompts.
   - Liveness of GPU nodes: gpuname reported and ready.

4) Safety and gating:
   - Run requires: explicit run_reason, operator approved toggle, and a TTL-limited run token.
   - IAM: least-privilege run role, assume-only for drill, no permanent route changes.
   - Time window constraint: drills allowed only in configured windows per tenant (configurable in module).

Acceptance criteria:
- Terraform modules pass static validation and unit tests (terratest).
- End-to-end rehearsal can be executed in a Redwood-managed sandbox account without human intervention (happy path).
- Drill harness produces a Drill Report artifact with metrics, logs, and a verdict (pass/fail) and uploads to S3 and Console.
- Auto-rollback is executed for at least one failure scenario in CI (simulate control-plane error).
- Docs: PRD + operator runbook + sample terragrunt configuration for customers.

Implementation plan / milestones:
- Week 1: Prototyping modules/drill-runner and traffic-generator, define validation rule DSL. (Owner: Aisha)
- Week 2: Implement health-checks module and a simple StepFunction prototype. Integrate with Prometheus/CloudWatch exporter. (Owner: Marco)
- Week 3: Implement safety gating and IAM role scoping; terratest harness for CI. (Owner: SRE pair)
- Week 4: E2E sandbox rehearsal and produce draft Console drill-view. (Owner: PM + Eng)
- Week 5: Internal stakeholder reviews (Security, Solutions Eng, Customer Success), iterate on safe defaults. (Owner: Product)

Rollout plan / communication:
- Beta: offer to 2-3 pilot customers with support from Solutions Eng; announce in private-customer channel.
- GA: include as an opt-in module in private-2026.1 with docs and training runbook.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Terraform modules perform irreversible networking changes. Mitigation: design modules to only create reversible temporary routes and to never alter customer persistent route tables without explicit two-step approval.
- Risk: Synthetic traffic might expose customer data or degrade production. Mitigation: require sandboxed traffic generator and configurable rate-limiting; run only in tenant-specified test subnets.
- Risk: Validation rules give false negatives/positives. Mitigation: expose rule thresholds, run shadow-mode for two cycles before enforcing rollback.

Test artifacts / references:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIVATE/Regional+Continuity+Simulator
- Initial design diagram: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1DRILL-ARCH-DIAG
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-drills/pull/42
- Terratest CI: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-drills/actions/workflows/terratest.yml
- Console mockup: https://figma.com/file/PrivateDrill/console-drill-view

Follow-ups / next steps:
- Expand provider support to GCP and Azure after initial AWS stabilization.
- Add automated verification of model invariants (SAMPLING/temperature checks) and semantic regression checks tied to eval harnesses.

Notes: This ticket should coordinate closely with Security (IAM review), Solutions Engineering (customer network patterns), and Console (drill UI). If successful, we will fold the modules into the Private onboarding template and add a recurring scheduled rehearsal feature in a follow-up ticket.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Modules/terraform validate + terratest passing in CI; 2) Running an automated rehearsal in sandbox completes end-to-end (preflight -> failover -> validation -> teardown) with artifacts; 3) Drill report stored in S3 and visible in Console mock; 4) Auto-rollback exercised in CI; 5) Security review sign-off
implementation_plan: See description milestones: prototype modules (week1), health checks + stepfunction (week2), safety gating + terratest (week3), e2e sandbox + console draft (week4), stakeholder reviews (week5). Coordinate PRs: private-drills/modules/* and private-drills/orchestrator/*
rollout_plan: Beta to 2-3 pilot customers with Solutions Eng support. GA as opt-in module in private-2026.1. Publish runbook and training session for Solutions Eng and SREs.
risks_mitigation: Design reversible changes only; require explicit operator approvals; sandbox traffic generator; shadow-mode validation rules before enforcement; least-privilege IAM roles and TTL-bound tokens.
